one_liner: All-in-one workspace for notes, wikis, docs, and databases used for team knowledge management and project tracking.
access_note: Internal integration tokens, OAuth public integrations, and personal access tokens can all be created free from the developer portal on any workspace including the Free plan.
api_breadth_note: Covers pages, databases/data sources, views, users, comments, file uploads, search, and webhooks across the whole workspace.
existing_mcp_note: Official Notion MCP is a remote, OAuth-authenticated MCP server hosted by Notion, with admin controls for connection management.

evidence.note: Overview of internal/public connections and personal access tokens.
Confirms official remote MCP server hosted by Notion.

researcher_notes: One of the strongest cases: broad REST API, fully self-serve auth, official hosted MCP server.

one_liner: Spreadsheet-database hybrid for building custom data tools, trackers, and lightweight apps.
access_note: Personal access tokens and OAuth apps can be created free at airtable.com/create/tokens without any approval step; legacy API keys were deprecated Feb 2024.
api_breadth_note: Covers bases, tables, records, fields/schema management, and webhooks, scoped by granular per-token permission scopes.
existing_mcp_note: Community package 'airtable-mcp-server' (npm) provides read/write MCP tools using a PAT; no official Airtable-branded MCP server found.

evidence.note: API overview and official/community client libraries.
Confirms PAT and OAuth as the two supported free, self-serve auth methods.

researcher_notes: No sign of an official Airtable MCP as of this research.

one_liner: Issue tracking and project management tool built for software teams.
access_note: Personal API keys and OAuth apps are created free directly in-app/developer console; no sales or partnership gate.
api_breadth_note: Covers issues, projects, cycles, comments, attachments, customers, and webhooks via a single GraphQL schema.
existing_mcp_note: Official remote MCP server (OAuth 2.1, dynamic client registration, also supports direct bearer-token/API-key auth), plus a read-only variant.

evidence.note: Developer portal confirming GraphQL API, OAuth2/API key auth, and TypeScript SDK.
Official MCP server docs with setup instructions.

researcher_notes: Linear also has a distinct 'AI Agents' framework separate from the MCP server.

one_liner: Issue and project tracking platform for software and business teams, part of Atlassian Cloud.
access_note: Free Atlassian Cloud accounts can generate API tokens for basic auth and register OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps in the developer console at no cost.
api_breadth_note: Very large REST v3 surface: issues, projects, workflows, permissions, JQL search, webhooks, fields, and more.
existing_mcp_note: Official Atlassian Rovo Remote MCP Server covers Jira and Confluence, OAuth-secured, with per-plan rate limits.

evidence.note: Jira Cloud REST API v3 reference landing page confirming huge endpoint coverage.
Official Rovo MCP server product page confirming all Cloud customers including Free plan have access.

researcher_notes: Atlassian discourages apps that just collect raw API tokens for third-party integrations, prefers a single distributable OAuth app.

one_liner: Work and task management platform for teams to plan, track, and coordinate projects.
access_note: Personal access tokens and OAuth apps are free/self-serve on any workspace; testing premium-tier features specifically requires requesting an approved developer sandbox (up to a week).
api_breadth_note: Covers tasks, projects, portfolios, custom fields, workspace events/webhooks, batch requests, and app components/UI builder.
existing_mcp_note: Official Asana MCP Server with a compatible-clients list and full MCP tools reference.

evidence.note: Developer platform overview confirming PAT/OAuth auth and listing the official MCP Server docs.
Confirms base API/PAT access is self-serve, while premium-feature sandboxes require an approval form.

researcher_notes: Core buildability is not blocked by the sandbox approval — that only matters for Enterprise/Advanced-only features.

one_liner: Customizable 'Work OS' for managing boards, workflows, projects, and automations.
access_note: Admin and member users can generate a personal API token for free instantly from the Developer Center; only Viewers/disabled/unconfirmed/student accounts are excluded.
api_breadth_note: Very large schema: boards, items, columns, workspaces, docs, dashboards, forms, automations, and a growing 'Platform MCP' tool catalog.
existing_mcp_note: Official 'Platform MCP' with dozens of documented tools, supporting API-token or OAuth app auth.

evidence.note: Confirms GraphQL API, who can use it, and lists official Platform MCP docs.
Confirms free, self-serve personal API token generation.

researcher_notes: monday.com's MCP surface is unusually extensive (workflow/automation/agent-management tools, not just CRUD).

one_liner: All-in-one productivity platform combining tasks, docs, chat, goals, and views.
access_note: The Public API is available on all plans including Free; a personal token is generated instantly in account settings, no approval needed.
api_breadth_note: Covers tasks, custom fields, views, comments, chat, docs, and webhooks; a small set of user/guest-management endpoints are Enterprise-only.
existing_mcp_note: Official ClickUp MCP Server with setup instructions and a supported-tools list.

evidence.note: Confirms free self-serve personal token generation and OAuth flow.
Confirms API is available on all plans, with only a narrow set of Enterprise-only endpoints.

researcher_notes: Clean, fully self-serve case with an official MCP server.

one_liner: Docs/spreadsheet/app hybrid ('all-in-one doc') for building team workflows and tools.
access_note: Coda's docs state the API is available free of charge to all users on both free and paid workspaces; a Bearer API token is generated from account settings.
api_breadth_note: Covers docs, pages, tables/rows, formulas, and controls — narrower than full workspace-admin platforms.
existing_mcp_note: Community package 'coda-mcp' (npm) wraps the Coda API for page/doc operations; no official Coda-branded MCP server found.

evidence.note: Coda API v1 docs confirming free availability and Bearer token auth.
Community MCP server implementation for Coda pages/docs.

researcher_notes: Coda's dedicated MCP subpage returned no content when fetched directly — unclear if Coda has since shipped an official MCP offering.

one_liner: Enterprise work management platform combining spreadsheet-style sheets with workflow automation, reports, and dashboards.
access_note: Smartsheet's own API introduction page states the required plan is Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management — the API is not available on free/personal tiers.
api_breadth_note: Covers sheets, rows/cells, folders, reports (recently full CRUD), dashboards, users, and asset-path/discovery endpoints.
existing_mcp_note: Official Smartsheet MCP Server with 30+ tools, documented and promoted directly alongside the REST API reference.
main_blocker: Requires a paid Smartsheet plan (Business/Enterprise/Advanced Work Management) to obtain any API access.

evidence.note: States required plan explicitly and links the Developer Agreement.
Confirms official MCP server and links to MCP server tools documentation.

researcher_notes: Plan-gating is the key differentiator vs the rest of this list.

one_liner: Time tracking and invoicing tool for services businesses and freelancers.
access_note: Harvest has a genuinely free-forever plan (1 seat, 2 projects); Personal Access Tokens and OAuth2 apps are created free on any account tier, no approval needed.
api_breadth_note: Covers time entries, projects, tasks, clients, invoices, expenses, and reports — focused on the time-tracking/billing domain.
existing_mcp_note: No official Harvest MCP server found in docs, and no well-known matching community package was located during this research.

evidence.note: API v2 documentation index covering all resource areas.
Confirms free self-serve Personal Access Tokens and OAuth2 app registration.

researcher_notes: MCP search was not exhaustive for Harvest — 'none_found' should be treated as 'nothing found in the search performed' rather than a fully exhaustive negative.
